_comment: Symbols scheduled for deletion by P9 (10-cleanup), consumed by scripts/verify/deadcode_report.php and the server-debug-deadcode API action. Sibling of expected_diffs.json / expected_command_diffs.json. A symbol is GREEN when it has ZERO blocking call sites: matches in its own defining file, under tests/, and in any path listed in its allowed_callers are not blocking. GREEN means 'safe to delete'; it is a PRECONDITION of the deletion, never a record that the deletion happened. KEYED BY NAME, NEVER BY LINE NUMBER -- the execution packs' line citations go stale within days, so this file deliberately carries no line numbers: there is exactly one thing to keep true, the symbol name and its declaring file.

_fields.allowed_callers: Path prefixes whose matches are reported but do not block. Three legitimate reasons only: (a) a documented external contract that keeps its callers (checkComponentPairCompatibility); (b) a NAME COLLISION the scan cannot resolve, because it matches method names without resolving the $this-> receiver to a class (extractPCIeSlotSize, checkFormFactorCompatibility); (c) a verification-harness call site under scripts/verify (see harness_call_sites_to_edit). Never allow-list a path to make a symbol go green without first reading why it matched, and always leave a note saying which reason applies.
_fields.internal_callers_also_deleted: Boolean, read at deadcode_scan.php:146. Declares that every SAME-FILE caller of this symbol is itself a manifest deletion target going in the same P9 commit -- i.e. the symbol sits inside a closed dead subgraph. Without it, same-file callers make the symbol RED_INTERNAL (deadcode_scan.php:190-196), which makes the gate unpassable for a private helper whose only callers are its own dead neighbours. NEVER set it when any same-file caller is LIVE code: validateComponentCompatibility, validateCPUAddition, validateRAMAddition, validateComponentQuantity and assignComponentSlot are all called from ServerBuilder::addComponent(), and validateConfiguration / validateConfigurationComprehensive are called from finalizeConfiguration() -- both reachable. Those must stay RED until their live call sites are removed. Setting this flag where the caller is live would greenlight deleting live validation: exactly the failure recorded in deadcode_report.php's header.
_fields.harness_call_sites_to_edit: Informational, read by no code. Verification-harness call sites (scripts/verify/**) that are allow-listed above and MUST be edited or removed in the same commit that deletes the symbol. A benchmark/report harness is not a production consumer, so it must not block the gate -- but it IS code that breaks when the symbol goes, so the obligation is recorded here instead of being discovered at run time.
_fields.sub_unit: Informational, read by no code. The finer P9 sub-session that owns the symbol, per U-D.2.md's SPLIT MANDATE (U-D.2a full-config validators + endpoint wire / U-D.2b add-path per-type validators / U-D.2c authority classes + pipeline / U-D.2d warnings + score family). Migrated from the orphaned scripts/verify/deadcode_targets.json on 2026-08-24. The `unit` field stays coarse so --unit=U-D.2 keeps selecting the whole set.

_marker_targets_note: deadcode_targets.json also carried U-D.4 'marker' entries (env-flag / TEMP-GUARD literals that must not survive). This scan has no marker kind -- deadcodeReferencePattern() understands only 'class' and 'method' -- so they cannot live here. They were migrated into migration/10-cleanup/execution-packs/U-D.4.md on 2026-08-24, which is the unit whose acceptance test greps for them.
_excluded_dirs_note: scripts/verify is deliberately NOT excluded, even though `scripts` is a scan root and the verify harness is not production code. Excluding the whole directory would silently hide a real production caller that ever lands there, and the exclusion would be invisible in the report. Harness call sites are instead exempted per symbol via allowed_callers + harness_call_sites_to_edit, so every exemption is named, reviewable, and carries its own follow-up obligation.

ComponentDataExtractor.php declares a THIRD, public copy but contains no call site, so it is deliberately not allow-listed -- re-check if that changes. PARTIALLY deleted 2026-08-30, then RETAINED. P9 removed what was actually superseded: validateAddition() (the add-time entry point, replaced by PcieLaneBudgetRule) and currentMode() (the PCIE_LANE_CHECK_ENABLED reader, removed by U-D.4). The ServerBuilder blocker went with legacyValidateComponentAddition(). What remains is NOT dead and was never superseded: StorageConnectionValidator::checkPCIeLaneBudget() calls evaluateAssembledStorageLaneBudget() on a live path, and ledger_report.php recomputes lane arithmetic against the same methods. The pre-2026-08-30 entry read retain:false, which was wrong -- deleting the class would have broken a live storage check. FLAGS.md's citation of currentMode() as the canonical flag-read pattern is moot: there are no flags left.

Zero callers of ServerBuilder's copy, pre-dating this change. Thin wrapper over checkFormFactorCompatibilityDetailed; deleting it drops that helper to GREEN. allowed_callers reason (b) NAME COLLISION, added 2026-08-24 following extractPCIeSlotSize's precedent: two DISTINCT methods share this name. ServerBuilder's is the dead wrapper `private function checkFormFactorCompatibility($components)` returning a score. ComponentCompatibility's is a LIVE `private function checkFormFactorCompatibility($storageSpecs, $motherboardSpecs, $existingStorage = [])` returning a verdict array, called from its own checkMotherboardStorageCompatibility(), which is reached by dynamic dispatch (`$this->$compatibilityMethod(...)`) through the 'motherboard-storage' / 'storage-motherboard' entries of getCompatibilityMethod()'s map. Different arity, different return shape, different class -- verified by hand 2026-08-24. The scan matches by name and cannot resolve the receiver, so that live namesake registered as the ONLY blocking caller of the dead wrapper and pinned it RED with no way to clear. DO NOT delete ComponentCompatibility's copy.
